newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Backstrom says Swedish ERM link needs public ok.
newsitem.headline: Backstrom says Swedish ERM link needs public ok.

text.p: Swedish central bank governor Urban Backstrom said Swedish participation in the European Union's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) was still not being considered and such a move demanded broad public support.

"We have made it perfectly clear that ERM membership is not being considered at present and will require broad support in Swedish society. To date, however, the reactions have been hesitant," Backstrom told a banking seminar in Frankfurt.
A copy of his speech was released by the central bank in Stockholm.
Backstrom said he was in favour of keeping the current fluctuation band of 15 percent intact for ERM2.

"The size of the standard fluctuation band in the ERM2 has still to be decided but, as I see it, the principles of continuity and equal treatment among all member states are important arguments for maintaining the current 15 percent."
Backstrom said the central bank, the Riksbank, had started a debate on the issue in the light of an improved economic situation in Sweden.

"The Riksbank has during this autumn, however, initiated a discussion about Swedish participation in the ERM in the context of the vigorous consolidation of government finance and the low level of inflation, together with the resultant improvement in the economic policy's credibility," Backstrom said.
